title: Contract SLA and Error Budget Framework for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Objective: Define a prescriptive, legally defensible SLA and error-budget model for Redwood Dedicated that maps throughput guarantees to contractual remedies, monitoring/measurement methodology, and operational controls. Scope includes: measurable SLA metrics (p95 latency, sustained throughput, request success rate), error budget math and consumption rules, blackout/exclusion windows, permissible throttling/fallback behavior, escalation and reporting cadence, and customer-visible contract language (SLA section + examples). This doc will be used by Sales/Legal for new Dedicated contracts and by Engineering/Support for runbooks and alerting.

Deliverables: 1) Formal SLA definitions and measurement spec, 2) Error budget calculation and burn policy, 3) Standard contract text (customer-facing SLA + credits matrix), 4) Implementation checklist (metrics instrumentation, dashboards, log exports), 5) Acceptance criteria for handoff to Legal and Sales Ops.

Key trade-offs discussed: tighter SLAs (higher availability/throughput) increase cost and capacity reservation needs; overly broad exclusions weaken customer trust. We propose a two-tier model (Committed Throughput SLA + Best-Effort Burst) with explicit fallback rules to minimize surprise for customers while preserving operational flexibility.

recommended_sla_spec: Metric A - Committed Throughput: measured as sustained tokens/sec aggregated per customer pool over 5-minute sliding windows. SLA guarantee expressed as 99.5% of 5-minute windows meeting committed throughput over a 30-day billing period.
Metric B - Request Success Rate: percentage of requests that return 2xx semantic responses (not partial/trimmed) within the function-level timeout. SLA guarantee: 99.9% success over billing period.
Metric C - P95 Token Latency: end-to-end token generation latency at 95th percentile for single-request path. SLA target: <= 150ms for small model profiles; different tiers defined per instance type.

Error Budget: For each SLA metric, monthly error budget = (1 - SLA%) * total measurement windows or requests. Budgets are tracked independently and consumed when a window/request violates the metric. Burn-rate policy: normalized to 30-day rolling window for alerting and a billing-period window for credits.

Credit Banding: automated credits applied when one or more SLA metrics breach thresholds across the billing period. Examples: <0.1% breach = no credit; 0.1-1% breach = 5% invoice credit; 1-5% breach = 20% invoice credit; >5% breach = 50% invoice credit (subject to max cap per contract).

Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (with 72h notice), customer misconfiguration, third-party provider outages, region-level emergency deemed force majeure, and deliberate throttling due to account misuse are excluded from credits. Any maintenance shorter than 60 minutes per calendar month is not considered a breach when disclosed.

Monitoring & Measurement: canonical metric names and labels will be emitted to the telemetry namespace (dedicated.sla.*). Measurement will use instrumentation at ingress and egress to capture tokens, duration, and error semantics. Rolling 30-day and calendar-month windows must both be supported for reporting.

Operational Controls: automatic graceful degradation policies (fallback to compatible model variant, rate-limited burst) are permitted if documented in contract. Fallbacks must be logged and surfaced to the customer via incident reports. Any fallback that materially reduces output quality for more than 10% of requests in the billing period counts against the Request Success Rate SLA unless explicitly accepted in contract.

Change Control: SLA changes require 30 days notice for existing customers and written acceptance in new contracts. For platform-level changes that affect all customers, Redwood will provide migration guidance and an optional transition credit for the first billing period after change.

Transparency & Reporting: monthly SLA report sent to account owner with metric breakdown, incidents that consumed error budget, and any applied credits. Real-time dashboard available to customers with 24h delayed data to prevent exploitation.
